result.summary: Escapes backslashes in the Tor control port `AUTHENTICATE` command when using `HASHEDPASSWORD` authentication. Also adds functional test coverage with a mock Tor control server verifying backslash and quote escaping.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core sends `AUTHENTICATE "<password>"` under `HASHEDPASSWORD` authentication but only escapes double quotes. Tor treats backslashes in quoted strings as escape characters according to the control specification, causing passwords containing backslashes to be corrupted or malform the command syntax, which fails authentication and prevents onion service creation.
evidence: PR description: 'Tested against Tor 0.4.9.12 with HashedControlPassword set for pa\ss"word\: on master bitcoind logs "tor: Authentication failed", with this change authentication succeeds and ADD_ONION creates the onion service.'
PR description notes that with '-torpassword=pa\ss"word\', master sends 'AUTHENTICATE "pa\ss\"word\"' whereas the fix sends 'AUTHENTICATE "pa\\ss\"word\\"'.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the code or test logic compared to the previous version (likely a rebase or commit message edit).
result.card: Escapes backslashes before quotes when transmitting -torpassword in the Tor control AUTHENTICATE command under HASHEDPASSWORD authentication. Currently, Bitcoin Core only escapes quotation marks, which causes Tor's control-spec QuotedString parser to treat backslashes as escape characters; this corrupts the password or breaks command syntax and prevents onion service creation. The author verified against Tor 0.4.9.12 that a password with backslashes fails authentication on master and succeeds with this patch.

risk.why: A mistake in escaping could cause Tor control port authentication to fail, preventing automatic Tor onion service setup.
